observations: Both published complete static SVGs rendered with distinct reaction, chemical and protein node styles and visible directed edges.
The graphs are dense, with edge crossings and crowded predicate labels; full-size zoom and linked evidence tables remain important for individual claims.
No clipped node boxes or missing rendered network were observed in these images.
limits: Static image inspection only; CUA reported no enabled browser surfaces. Browser interaction, mobile layout, dark mode and hover tooltip behavior were not tested.
Dense edge crossings and predicate-label crowding remain; existing full-size controls and evidence tables provide individual-claim detail.
final_comparison_method: Compared final SVG with the actually inspected raster input after normalizing the content-hash namespace used by SVG IDs and their references, and removing nonvisual title/description/data-/aria- metadata. Every visible text, path, class, style and link otherwise compares byte-identically.
method_note: An initial direct equality attempt failed because content-hash SVG namespaces changed with evidence locators. Their ID/reference relationships were retained in the normalized comparison; no geometry was altered.
publication_scope: Only the two admitted degradation record pages. The earlier inspected staph image is historical and excluded from publication.
